messages.author: 3126d00d0b94540e
messages.subject: Convergence criteria
parts:
I have what is probably an ill-determined random effects model which does not always converge. I have a two part question.
How can I relax the convergence criteria (in nlminb)?

The error message when the minimizer gives up is a bit spartan:
Error in newton(par = c(logbeta = -7.44239271957212, logbeta = -7.43808037040032,  :
  Newton failed to find minimum.
So, is it possible get a "snapshot" of the parameter and random effects estimates when the minimizer gives up?

Thanks,
John

messages.author: 4453e5ef4c1cb06e
messages.subject: Re: Convergence criteria
parts: Hi John, nlminb has a control argument which has tolerance specifications. I'd also try setting trace=1 to see console updates of fixed effects. I think if you pull out obj$env$last.par it will give you the last parameter vector evaluated (fixed and random effects). You could rebuild the obj without random effects and put that back through to get the joint likelihood and maybe something obvious would pop out? I assume that message means the inner optimizer failed. Lastly, I'd run the model through tmbstan to see if full MCMC integration helps diagnose issues. -Cole
